title: statespace IR, version 1
description: The one JSON IR that links S3, S6 and S9 (spine section 9.3), written by `lake exe export-ir` and read by the TypeScript interpreter, the Lane A host and the Rust crates. TODO(W2-T08): this is the skeleton W0-T02 reserves. It fixes the envelope and the parts that curriculum/S03-semantics.md names (the policy fields of decision 6, and a golden's fields in section 2.7); the encodings of programs, calls, states and outcomes are open objects until W2-T08 publishes IR@1 from the Lean reference semantics. Narrowing an open object to a closed one is a compatible change for a writer that already emits only the narrowed form.

programs.description: Mini-Plinth programs: commands with distinct names.

calls.description: Calls of a command with raw argument values.

states.description: States: balances, holds, nextHold and flags.

policy.description: The edge-case decisions the semantics takes, which the learner's evaluator declares as Lab3.policy.

outcomes.description: Outcomes: ok with state, output and effects, or an Err with payload.

goldens.description: Kernel-checked goldens. Each right-hand side comes from the golden module's literals, never from a fresh #eval.

program.description: TODO(W2-T08): the encoding of a program.

call.description: TODO(W2-T08): the encoding of a call.

state.description: TODO(W2-T08): the encoding of a state.

outcome.description: TODO(W2-T08): the encoding of an outcome.

policy.description: The four policy fields of curriculum/S03-semantics.md section 1.1, decision 6. The reference defaults are zero reject, self allow, guard error and overflow unbounded.

zero.description: What an amount of 0 does: reject it, or return the state unchanged.

self.description: Whether a move from an account to itself is allowed or rejected.

guard.description: What a false guard gives: an error, or the state unchanged with no output.

overflow.description: Unbounded balances, or balances bounded to [-maxBal, maxBal]. TODO(W2-T08): confirm the encoding against the export.

golden.description: One golden: a theorem about a call on a pre-state, with its outcome.

pool.description: The golden pool the golden belongs to.

theorem.description: The Lean theorem name that proves the golden.

statementSha256.description: The statement hash of the theorem's text, by the rule of statement-hash@1.
